title: POC Weekly Sync - Quality Eval
summary: Weekly POC sync to review quality eval results, discuss regressions on new prompt set, propose guardrail adjustments, and agree next steps for a focused benchmark run and security paperwork.
next_steps: Alex to share updated prompt set + scoring spreadsheet by 2025-12-01
Liam to run regression tests on latest anonymized dataset (10k queries) and report metrics by 2025-12-03
Samir to schedule a 2-hour deep-dive for kernel/latency tuning with Nimbus infra team week of 12/08
Marco to confirm required SOC2 artifacts and initial onboarding questionnaire answers by 2025-12-05
action_items: Alex Morgan - send pilot pricing and pilot terms (incl. dedicated seat options) - due 2025-12-02
Samir Patel - update guardrail rule set (1/3 throttles, 2/3 soft-fail) and share playbook - due 2025-12-01
Liam Chen - run end-to-end regression (precision/recall + hallucination checks) and upload results - due 2025-12-03
Marco Ruiz - provide list of internal auditors & compliance contacts - due 2025-12-05
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're on the weekly POC sync to walk through the quality eval results from last week
[00:12] Priya (Nimbus PM): Thanks Alex, appreciate it. Quick note, Marco had to jump on late so he'll be joining in a few.
[00:20] Samir (Redwood SE): Hi all, Samir here. I'll run through the scoring summary then we can dig into examples.
[00:28] Liam (Nimbus ML): Cool, we've got the 10k anonymized set ready, just want to see where regressions happened after the prompt tweaks.
[00:36] Alex: Perfect. Samir, can you give an overview of the headline metrics?
[00:40] Samir: Yeah -- overall accuracy by their scoring rubric is 86% which is up from 82% two weeks ago on the baseline prompts, precision on the clinical extraction tasks is 0.88, recall 0.81. But importantly we did see a regression in the triage intent classification on short queries, down from 0.92 to 0.84.
[01:05] Priya: That's the one we were worried about. Could that be because of the new guardrail paraphrase we added?
[01:12] Samir: Possibly; the change to the prompt introduced an additional clarifying instruction which seems to bias the model toward conservative answers. Some of the short queries are now being marked as "unsure" where previously they'd be confidently assigned an intent.
[01:26] Liam: Do you have specific examples?
[01:28] Samir: Yes, I pulled three representative cases. Example A: input "fever and cough 2 days" used to map to "low-risk respiratory" and now gets "requires clinician triage" with a lower confidence score. Example B: "headache after vaccine" used to be vaccine-related triage, now flagged as "unsure".
[01:50] Priya: Hmm okay. For our UX we prefer recall over precision for triage -- false positives are okay if we can route to a nurse.
[01:58] Alex: Noted. So we need to tune prompt + guardrail to move recall back up without losing the gains in extraction accuracy.
[02:05] Samir: Right. A couple notes: the extraction tasks benefited from adding an explicit output schema and stronger examples, which helped token alignment for the entity spans. The triage classifier relies more on short-context cues which the schema changes inadvertently suppressed.
[02:22] Marco (Nimbus Security): Sorry I'm on. Quick question from security: are we retaining logs for more than 30 days in the POC environment? The compliance team is asking.
[02:30] Alex: For the hosted pilot we default to 30 days, but we can configure retention and we also support private deployment options — you can bring your own KMS.
[02:40] Marco: Good, we'll want the KMS/HSM details and the SOC2 docs.
[02:45] Alex: I'll share the SOC2 summary and the onboarding questionnaire after the call.
[02:49] Samir: Back to the evals -- we noticed two classes of hallucination on the discharge summary prompts: (1) invented medication dosages, (2) erroneous timeline inference. Those are down overall vs baseline but still present in 1.4% of cases.
[03:05] Liam: 1.4% could be material for downstream workflows, can we add a calibrated hallucination filter?
[03:11] Samir: Yes, we have two levers: output-level guardrails (post-hoc checks against the schema and a lightweight knowledge assertion), and routing to a safer, higher-cost model when the confidence or check fails. Both are configurable per-route.
[03:24] Priya: Routing sounds good but cost will be a concern. How often did the route fallback trigger in the run?
[03:30] Samir: In the 10k run fallbacks would have triggered for about 2.1% of tokens under the current confidence threshold. That would increase cost by roughly 6-8% given our batching profile.
[03:45] Alex: We should discuss acceptable SLOs with Priya's team; maybe do a soft-fail first where we surface potential issues to the UI rather than routing.
[03:53] Priya: Soft-fail seems like a pragmatic first step.
[03:57] Olivia (Data Ops): Quick question on the scoring: are the annotators internal to Nimbus or a mix? We're seeing some label noise.
[04:04] Liam: Mostly internal with a small external validation set. We suspected some label drift on the vaccine intent.
[04:11] Samir: We can re-weight the validation set and run an adjudication pass. Also worth adding a synthetic perturbation set to stress short queries.
[04:21] Alex: Can you outline the exact changes you'll make to the prompt? Samir?
[04:25] Samir: Sure. Plan A: revert the clarifying sentence that reduced short-context signals, instead inject a micro-prompt that emphasizes "if the user lists only symptoms and duration, prefer recall and output a triage label". Plan B: keep the clarifying sentence but widen the context window by including top-2 previous messages in prefix cache.
[04:44] Liam: Plan A sounds simpler and quicker. We can test both though.
[04:49] Samir: I'll prepare a diff of the prompt text and run the 10k set on both variants and provide precision/recall/hallucination numbers.
[04:57] Priya: Great. On metrics, can we get per-intent confusion matrices and model-calibrated confidence distributions?
[05:04] Samir: Yep, will include confusion matrices and reliability diagrams.
[05:08] Marco: Security question re: routing to higher-cost model — does that still expose patient data to a different environment? We need end-to-end data flow documented.
[05:15] Alex: With Redwood Dedicated or Private you control where the fallback model runs; with hosted we can pin fallbacks to our vetted instances and ensure encryption-in-transit and at-rest. We'll document the flow.
[05:26] Olivia: Also, can we mask PHI in the logs? We prefer redaction at the edge.
[05:31] Samir: We have prefix-level masking as part of the SDK and you can enable client-side PII redaction before payloads hit the runtime. We'll share the SDK snippet.
[05:40] Priya: Back to the UX: when the system is "unsure" we show a soft-hint to the nurse, correct?
[05:45] Liam: Yes, soft-hint + escalation path. We're okay tuning thresholds that produce more hints.
[05:51] Alex: Next: latency. We saw a small uptick when we enabled schema constraining, average tail p95 went from 320ms to 380ms. Samir, is that expected?
[06:01] Samir: Yes, schema enforcement adds a small decoding overhead and we also saw slightly smaller batch sizes due to short query distribution which impacts throughput. We can reduce the p95 by enabling continuous KV cache and also tuning kernel selection; small wins on CUDA kernel settings gave us 40-50ms improvement in other pilots.
[06:18] Priya: If we tune kernels, will that require changes to our infra?
[06:22] Samir: No infra change for hosted; for private we can coordinate with your infra team for GPU driver compatibility. That's why we recommended the deep-dive next week.
[06:31] Alex: Proposed timetable: Samir runs prompt variants and uploads results by 2025-12-01; Liam runs regression and shares any label adjustments by 2025-12-03; Alex to send SOC2 + KMS docs and pricing by 2025-12-02.
[06:45] Priya: Sounds good. A couple more quick items: can we get an export of the hallucination examples for our clinical review board?
[06:52] Samir: Yes, we'll produce a redacted example set and include source signals and token-level confidence.
[06:58] Marco: Also need the onboarding questionnaire answers; I'll coordinate offline with Alex.
[07:04] Alex: Okay thanks everyone. Any other questions?
[07:07] Olivia: One last ask -- can you include cost projections for enabling fallbacks at 1%, 2%, and 5% fallback rates?
[07:13] Alex: We'll include that in the pricing note.
[07:16] Priya: Thanks, that's all from me.
[07:18] Liam: Thanks.
[07:20] Alex: Thanks team, we'll follow up with the action items.
[07:24] [call ends]
